rules_text:
Rules summary There are two factions in Secret Moon (three when played with the Thief ). Blue Team: Minister and Guards : their goal is to either capture the Princess or reveal both the Princess and Wanderer. x4 Guards (cannot capture but can look for and reveal other players' roles) x1 Minister (is able to act as a guard but can also capture the Princess) (Blue team loses if Minister is captured) Red Team: Princess , Wanderer and Priestess . They win if the Minister is captured or if the Princess and/or Wanderer stay hidden until the end. x1 Princess (may look at, reveal and capture other players)(Red team loses if Princess is captured) x1 Wanderer (may look at, reveal and capture other players)(Red team loses if both Princess and Wanderer are revealed) x1 Priestess (may look at, reveal and capture other players) One match goes over three rounds, during each round the following actions are available: Inspect : secretly look at another player's character card. Inquire : ask "Who goes there?" to another player. This will give a clue about this player's identity. The Princess and the Wanderer will answer "..." when asked about their identity, while the Priestess and Guards will answer "It's just me." The Minister answers "You fool! I'm the Minister!" Accuse : guess a character card and reveal it (if incorrect, reveal your own). Note : when Guards are revealed, they are automatically captured. Protect : defend someone or yourself (unavailable during round 3). Disrupt : force another player to discard their turn order card (in exchange, you are captured). Capture : capture a player with a revealed character (Guards can only capture a thief). Pass : choose a discarded turn order card and take it (for the next round). Thief : The Thief is an optional third faction. He tries to avoid being captured until the end. The Thief cannot protect himself nor can he use Capture . All characters including guards can "Capture" you. When inquired about his identity, he can choose to answer like the Princess or the Minister. The Thief wins alone if he is not captured by the end of the game. However, NPC thief cannot win. For example: the Princess gets captured, but the Thief (not an NPC) is still alive. The Thief wins and is the only one to receive a victory point.

community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] One of Seiji Kanai's biggest stinkers.  An attempt to make a social deduction game for people who are bad at them. You're only allowed to say one specific line of dialogue, and that is really boring and doesn't make a fun social game experience for anyone. More an exercise in patience than a game at all.  Culled

[Rating: 2/10] It's a social game which for some idiotic reason deletes the social aspect: you can look at other people's cards but not reveal that information, or reveal their role (and risk your own team), or accuse them of being bad guys (which literally does nothing). Plus while it says 5-8 players, it really only works with 7-8. Really bad.

[Rating: 3/10] We played this a few times with 5 players. With 5 players, it makes abig difference whether the priestress is in the game or not. A big minus is the random player order, a lot of games are simply decided by that on the last turn. It might play way better with 7 or 8 people.

[Rating: 3/10] Very light, without enough substance to make it qualify as a game i would be interested in.

[Rating: 3/10] Game is good, but it only works fine if all the players really know how to play the game.

[Rating: 3.5/10] Very random, the turn sequence decides with team wins in about 50% of the games. If you don’t get a small number, you have no options at all. I cannot recommend it.

[Rating: 4/10] Like The Resistance but without the discussions, since there are pre-determined questions and answers for the roles. Quick to play.
